dish_name: Baked Salmon with Lemon and Dill
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Squeeze 2 tbsp of juice from one of the lemons. Finely chop 2 tbsp of the dill, mince the 1 tbsp capers and finely mince the garlic clove.

In a small bowl, stir together the 1/3 cup Greek yogurt, 3 tbsp mayonnaise, the 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp of the chopped dill, the capers, the garlic and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Put the bowl in the fridge.
Pat the 1.25 lb salmon dry with paper towels and cut it into 4 pieces if it came as one. Set the pieces skin side down on the lined sheet with space between them.
Sprinkle the salmon with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper and drizzle the 2 tsp olive oil over the top.
Cut the second lemon into 8 thin slices and lay 2 slices on each piece of salmon.

Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, depending on how thick the pieces are. You're cooking it to 140°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Press the thickest part with a fork: it's done when it flakes and is only just opaque in the middle.
Scatter the last 1 tbsp of chopped dill over the salmon. Taste the sauce, and add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of what's left of the first lemon if it's flat.
Serve the salmon with the lemon dill sauce spooned over the top, with rice or roast potatoes.
method_notes: All three bake salmon with lemon and fresh dill on a lined sheet for 15 minutes or less at 325 to 400°F. The Endless Meal (the only one with 20 or more ratings) bakes 5 oz fillets at 400°F for 8 to 10 minutes to 140°F with olive oil and lemon slices on top, and serves them with a cold sauce of Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, dill, capers and garlic. Six Sisters' Stuff spoons a lemon, garlic and dill butter over a whole fillet and bakes it sealed in foil at 375°F; Well Seasoned Studio scatters lemon zest and dill over a side of salmon and bakes it low, at 325°F, to 120°F. This one follows The Endless Meal and keeps a little dill back to scatter over the fish at the end.
